title: microplaybook-seller-ops-oncall-war-room-cheat-sheets-iter-alpha
content:
Purpose:
A compact, high-velocity reference for seller + ops oncall war rooms during pilot and early production incidents. Lightweight slide deck + 1p cheat sheets for quick distribution to SEs, platform sellers, and oncall ops engineers.

Audience (primary):
- Field SEs running pilot demos
- Platform/ops oncall responding to latency/cost/regression alerts
- Technical account owners who need one-pager quick answers

Tone and constraints:
- 60–90s read per card; verbal scripts for 30–60s openings
- Not exhaustive: prioritize safe fallback, customer reassurance, and next-step asks
- Include links to canary checklists, runbooks (but keep on-card actionable)

Core narrative frames (short):
1) Reassure -> Diagnose -> Remediate -> Commit
   - Short script: "We see elevated latency; we’ll route to a lower-cost variant while we investigate. I’ll follow up with timeline and mitigation."
2) Economics-first pitch when cost is concern:
   - "We can immediately enable prefix caching + a smaller model variant with 0 config changes on client side; that cuts unit costs by ~40% and keeps 95p latency near SLA."
3) Resilience story for regulators/enterprises:
   - "We run primary in-region + cross-region fallback; we can ship audit logs for the transaction window within 24h."

Battlecards (short cards for war room) — each card = 1 slide + 1p cheat:
- Symptom: "Sudden 3x token cost spike"
  - Quick checks: increased sequence length, model variant change, spike in retries/400s
  - Immediate action: temporarily pin older quantized model, enable batching cap, escalate to runtime oncall if persistent
  - Script: "We’ll pin to a validated quantized variant and throttle burst policies for 15m; expect cost to revert, I’ll update status in 10m."

- Symptom: "Latency P95 breached in production"
  - Quick checks: regional saturation, HV requests, KV cache miss rate, kernel fallback logs
  - Immediate action: reroute to second-tier pool (lower concurrency), enable prefix cache, scale a hot-pod (if dedicated)
  - Script: "We’re routing a portion of traffic to an alternate capacity tier and turning on prefix caching — this should recover p95 within minutes."

- Symptom: "Model quality regression (user visible) during rollout"
  - Quick checks: rollout delta, eval set scoring, prompt changes, prompt templating errors
  - Immediate action: quick rollback to last good version, enable canary traffic at 1% while we run an automated eval set, file a drift ticket
  - Script: "We rolled back the rollout to the previous model; we’ll run a 50-example eval set and share results in 30m."

Slide outline (compact deck for the field — 6 slides):
1) Cover: One-liner + intended audience + contact (SE + ops alias)
2) When to open the war room: trigger list + Slack channel template
3) Three most-common symptoms + 30s scripts (cards)
4) Quick triage checklist (network, model, runtime, customer prompts)
5) Safe fallback playbook (pin model, reroute, quantize, cache toggles)
6) Post-incident actions + customer follow-up template + tickets to raise

Scripts & Shortlines (copy-ready for SEs):
- Opening: "We’re seeing X; we’ll temporarily move to Y and investigate the root cause — ETA 15m for first update."
- CFO/Procurement: "We can cap spend at route level and provide a variance report for the billing window; ops will follow up with a cost breakdown."
- Platform engineer: "If you want to opt for a lower-latency profile we can pin to NVDLA-optimized kernels or throttle concurrency — which would you prefer?"

Operational knobs cheat (one-liners for war-room):
- Pin model: config -> model_version: 1.2.3 -> rollout: 100%
- Reroute: routing_policy -> prefer: variant-b, percent: 40
- Cache: prefix_cache -> enable:true ttl: 300s
- Quantize: q4_0 recommended for throughput-sensitive inference
- Batch caps: max_batch_size: 32 -> reduce to 8 if latency spike persists

Open questions (need input before v0.2):
- Do we commit to a standard 15m SLA for public updates during incidents? (Ops + GTM decision)
- Which team owns the customer-facing cost variance report (finance + CS?)
- Should we publish a small CLI snippet SEs can run to surface runtime logs for triage? (security review needed)

Next steps & owners (quick):
- Draft 6-slide deck + 3 one-pagers by Nov 12 — owner: Priya (this doc)
- Ops to validate the pinned-config quick commands and share runbook links — owner: Liam O'Connor — due Nov 1
- Create a Slack template and war-room alias; SEs to trial on next pilot — owner: Sofia Martinez — due Nov 5

Notes to self / rough brainstorm:
- Keep cards offline-printable as 3-up on single sheet for in-person briefings
- Consider embedding a tiny flowchart graphic with arrowed actions (reassure -> pin -> reroute -> escalate)
- Shortlist 5 customer-facing phrases approved by legal for external updates

Fragmented ideas / stash:
- "Economics quick calc" snippet: tokens/sec * p50_latency * unit_cost -> quick estimate to hand to CFO
- Mini-FAQ for pilots: "Will you change our model?" -> "Only with your signoff; we can use variant routing to test."

Status: rough draft. Want to keep lightweight and usable in 1–2 pager forms. Will iterate with ops after internal dry-run on Nov pilot.

-- Priya
